recipes.name: Creamed Cabbage
ingredients_raw: 1 large head cabbage, cored and shredded

steps.text: Cook bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate.

Add butter, flour, and salt to the skillet; whisk with drippings over medium heat until butter melts. Add cabbage and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender, about 15 minutes. Crumble bacon into the skillet. Stir in sour cream and cook until heated through, 1 to 2 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamed Cabbage
raw_recipe.description: Creamed cabbage with crispy bacon, shredded cabbage, and tangy sour cream is a super easy side dish you'll want to serve for St. Patrick's Day.

video.description: This video shows you how to make quick, creamy cabbage flavored with bacon and sour cream. Incredibly simple, it’s terrific for St. Patrick’s Day and, paired with pork chops or roasts, makes a great side dish any time.

review.reviewBody: very good! I only used half a head of cabbage & kept the other ingredients the same, It turns out more creamy that way! I also carmelized a small chopped onion & added it to the mix. Lastly, I transfered it to a baking dish, topped with panko bread crumbs and baked @350 for about 10 min.

This was really, really good! It's the middle of summer and cabbage is chep but hubby doesn't like coleslaw and corned beef and cabbage doesn't seem right in July so I tried this recipe and between 2 adults, 1 teen and 2 toddlers we polished off the whole big bowl! Now I did add an extra strip of bacon cause c'mon, it's bacon! but aside from that I followed the recipe exactly and sooo good, everyone loved it!

Loved this dish. I live on my own and in the Netherlands where we grow a lot of cabbage. This dish was a great one pot dish with plenty of leftovers to play with. I didnt use bacon but used finely diced ham instead, adding a little oil to replace the loss of bacon fat. Heated some up the next day for lunch and threw in a handfull of leftover rice. Yummy!!

My family loved this recipe, even my 6yr old who doesnt like to eat his veggies. I didnt have any sour cream so I substituted with 1 cup of evaporated milk mixed with 1 tbsp vinegar. Came out perfect!

Awesome! Like other reviewers, I added onion and garlic. All I had was a pound of turkey bacon so I didn't have any grease. I added 1/2 C of butter & deglazed the pan then added the cabbage, onion & garlic. I added pepper and smoked paprika for great color. I added the full pound of diced turkey. Will definitely make again!

My adjustments were so numerous as to make it a different recipe but I did build upon it (smile). Like most others, I used half a head of cabbage. First I sautéed a large onion and minced garlic. I used a cup of chopped ham, used a cup of cream and spiced with two tsps of tarragon, kosher salt and pepper both to taste and added a tsp of sweet paprika.

Will definitely make this again. I used gluten free flour with no problem. For personal preference, I sauteed onion with the cabbage and pepper with the flour and salt, and I wouldn't change a thing. So easy, quick, and yummy!

KETO VERSION: omit the flour. I used leftover bacon fat because I was out of bacon so I fried up some chopped salami, after I had halfway sautéed cabbage... at the end I stirred in about quarter cup or so of sour cream and it’s pretty darn good ALSO sprinkled on some garlic salt and pepper for flavour

the absolute best I've ever made...i loved adding flour to make it slightly creamy...we will make this way from now on...i followed to as written only i was out of bacon..i used stored bacon fat and added ham chunks to the bacon oil also assed onion's then the flour...browned nicely, added chicken broth then cabbage...

I've made this twice. First time I followed the recipe and it was great. The second time I *thought* I had bacon and didn't! So I pulled some country ham pieces from the freezer, cooked those up and cut them into small pieces. No "grease" to speak of, but that didn't cause any issues and it was delicious!!

I used a package of bacon cooked this and half cup of Tasso. I then took an onion and cook the onion and the bacon fat. Didn't use all the bacon just the bacon fat. Then I followed the rest of the recipe and used a whole head of cabbage and a cup of light sour cream. Someone else had recommended putting breadcrumbs on top and I did this but I think it's better to mix it with a little butter and toast it and then put it on top rather than put it in the oven because my bread crumbs never toasted. I ended up just mixing it in and it tasted great but if you wanted that breadcrumb topping look then make sure you mix it with some better something. It's not a healthy recipe at all but it taste great

I used my electric wok to make the cabbage part of it and a microwave bacon tray to cook the bacon. Made it all extra easy. I'll bet the dish tastes even better tomorrowm like many vegetable recipes do.
We like spicy so I added a can of hot green chilies and I added half of a chopped white onion. Like others, I increased the bacon to 6 slices. So good, we will definitely make this again.

Never had creamed cabbage before, but we’re now fans. I didn’t mix the crisp bacon into the cabbage with the sour cream because it would become soggy; just sprinkled it on top. This doesn’t really get creamy with just the sour cream, although its flavor is there. The consistency was just about perfect for us.
Followed as written but made with red cabbage and no bacon as my husband is vegetarian. Very good comfort food. Will make again!
I didn’t think that the flour was necessary but I followed the recipe and it turned out great…nice and creamy, not greasy at all!

My husband really liked this and complimented several times while eating. I liked-okay. Settling on a 4 since he would love if I made again but the tang on the sour cream is just not the creamed cabbage I am accustomed - which is okay! I halved the recipe entirely EXCEPT the bacon and then added some chopped onions to the cabbage sauté. Glad I tried & thanks for sharing!
Like some others I used half a head of cabbage. Also used 6 pieces of bacon, and was generous with both the butter and sour cream. Really delicious, and really great on a keto lifestyle!
Much too rich for our taste, but I don’t like carbonara dishes either.

I tweaked the recipe by adding some freshly ground black pepper, a wee bit more bacon and butter. I made this for our main dinner, and not a side dish. We love cabbage just about any way it can be cooked. This was easy to make. Only wish we had had some good, hard rolls to eat with this dish. Yes, we love our carbs.
